reasoning:
The reproduction runs and its literal output is correct. The conclusion drawn from it does not follow, and the one mechanism that could have rescued it is measurably absent.

(1) WHAT THE GATE ACTUALLY GRADES. holdout.py:251-265 loads each holdout board's RAW CSV, converts it to (percentile, value/top*9999) pairs via _percentile_pairs (:131-145), and takes the RMSE of the Hill curve against those pairs (:161-162). The criterion is a shape comparison between a candidate (c,s) pair and a source's OWN PUBLISHED value curve. It never reads the blended board, rankDerivedValue, or any pipeline output. So 'the benchmark is not independent of the board it grades' is a category error: the thing graded is a curve, and the board the finding means is downstream of and invisible to the criterion.

(2) THE INFERENCE IS BACKWARDS. Those four sources vote via rank -> percentile -> Hill. A curve that reproduces FantasyCalc's published value shape converts FantasyCalc's rank vote into a value closer to what FantasyCalc actually says. That is a MORE faithful translation of the vote, not a more circular one. And the failure the gate exists to catch — overfitting to the six training boards — remains fully detectable: the four holdout CSVs have their own decay shapes (measured above, RMSE 881-1933 apart from KTC) whether or not they are also registry entries. Registry membership changes nothing about the quantity computed.

(3) THE FantasyNavigator LEG — the strongest part of the finding — IS MEASURABLY FALSE. The finding argues fantasyNavigatorSf carries correlation_group='ktc' (true; I confirmed both the field and the registry comment 'FN's values are KTC-derived ... documented here so nobody reads FN agreement with KTC as independent confirmation'), so a KTC derivative sits in the holdout set while holdout.py:69-73 excludes ktcSfTep for exactly that reason. I tested the contamination on the quantity the gate actually computes. FN's normalized percentile->value curve is the FURTHEST from KTC's of all nine boards (1933.2) — further than every training board, further than the other three holdouts. The per-player provenance is KTC-derived; the value SHAPE, which is the only thing scored, is not. Empirically FN is the board that most PENALIZES a KTC-shaped curve (its per-source RMSE is the worst in every recorded verdict: 1185.15 on v1, 1148.53 on v2). It is not smuggling KTC back in; it is the strictest board in the set.

(4) THE claimUnderTest IS A STRAWMAN. The finding says 'the word held-out is used throughout to mean independent'. holdout.py:33-40 says the opposite in its own words: 'It does NOT measure accuracy against reality. Every holdout source is another consensus market, correlated with the training sources by construction — they price the same players off the same news. There is no ground truth...'. That text is not a comment only — it is serialized into EVERY recorded verdict as `_semantics.doesNotMeasure` (:193-203), alongside criterionName 'mean_per_source_rmse'. The finding's own requiredRepair option (b), 'rename the criterion to what it measures — cross-market shape agreement', is already done in the module and in config/model_registry/hill_scope_masters.json.

(5) THE LITERAL CLAIM UNDER TEST IS TRUE. 'The fit never reads the holdout boards': scripts/fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:59-71 OFFENSE_SOURCES contains exactly the six training entries, pinned against holdout.OFFENSE_TRAINING_SOURCES by tests/model_registry/test_refit_path_characterisation.py:193-209. No holdout CSV is in the fit.

(6) BLAST RADIUS IS FABRICATED AND SELF-CONTRADICTED. The record claims playersAffected 1092 / routesAffected 100 / pagesAffected 38 while its own userImpact says 'Nothing a user sees changes today'. Both cannot be true. Today: 0 players, 0 routes, 0 pages carry a wrong number from this. The gate is a CI quality gate on a script-only path with a human promote step (ADR-008).

RESIDUAL, recorded so it is not lost: there IS a policy asymmetry worth a P3 doc note — holdout.py excludes ktcSfTep by name for KTC-derivation but includes fantasyNavigatorSf, which the same repo labels correlation_group='ktc'. I measured that asymmetry to have no effect on the criterion, so it is an inconsistency in stated policy, not a defective benchmark. That is a different, far smaller finding than the one filed.

Context I confirmed while trying to save the finding (it does not rescue it): the gate is genuinely live and has genuinely moved production constants — config/model_registry/hill_scope_masters.json shows v1 (crit 819.73) retired, v2 (787.84) promoted 2026-07-29, v3 (775.05) recorded as rejected. So had the contamination been real, the impact would have been serious. It is not real.

correctedBlastRadius.note: Nothing user-facing. Residual is a P3 documentation/policy-consistency note on holdout.py:69-79 (ktcSfTep excluded for KTC-derivation, fantasyNavigatorSf included despite correlation_group='ktc') — measured to have zero effect on the criterion.

whatWouldSettleIt: It is settled against the finding. The only thing that could revive the blend-membership argument would be a demonstration that the criterion reads a pipeline OUTPUT rather than each source's raw CSV — holdout.py:251-265 shows it does not. Reviving the FN leg would require showing FN's normalized percentile->value curve is close to KTC's; measured, it is the furthest of all nine boards.

reasoning:
The core is real and I strengthened it with evidence the finding did not have. Three of its stated numbers are wrong, and its status label is wrong by the protocol's own vocabulary. Rescoped, not upheld as written.

WHAT SURVIVES (verified independently):
- src/news/unified_signal_engine.py has ZERO production importers. Every hit is a comment or docstring. Confirmed exactly as stated.
- /api/consensus-edge/top -> 503 feature_disabled; /board and /summary are 404 (only one route exists). The arbiter is unreachable. Per AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md the 503 itself is a non-finding but 'reachability is the claim to test' — that is what this claims, so it is admissible.
- Multiple unreconciled emitters, and the disagreement is LIVE and user-visible. I measured it rather than asserting it: on the running contract, 90 players — including Brock Bowers (rank 2) and Bijan Robinson (rank 3) — get a BUY/SELL verb in PlayerPopup (getPlayerEdge, >=3, trade-logic.js:949, rendered at PlayerPopup.jsx:666 which appears on every page, plus trade-sections.jsx:559/666 and the /league Edge Map via league-analysis.js:933) while the /rankings Edge column for the same player is blank (marketAction, >=10, rankings/page.jsx:1166). A further 50 carry a backend direction stamp no UI ever surfaces. That is a concrete contradiction on reachable pages with no warning.

WHAT IS WRONG:
(a) 'FIVE competing threshold sets on the SAME retail-vs-consensus quantity' — it is THREE. Verified in source: >0 (data_contract.py:3051), >=3 (trade-logic.js:949), >=10 (thresholds.js:46). The 4th entry gates on `sourceRankSpread` — cross-source DISPERSION, a different quantity — which the finding's own family record #4 concedes ('marketGapDirection for DIRECTION, sourceRankSpread for GATE and SORT'). The 5th, idpMarketAction, is not a competing threshold at all: display-helpers.js:370 imports the SAME MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF constant and applies it to the IDP market. It is the one pair in the whole set that IS consistent, and per-market separation of the retail anchor is documented policy (CLAUDE.md, finder.py per-market gate). Counting the one consistent case as evidence of inconsistency is the opposite of what it shows.
(b) status 'Missing' is wrong by AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md's own vocabulary ('Missing — no code exists'), which the protocol explicitly flags as the distinction most often botched at scale. Both candidate arbiters exist. unified_signal_engine is textbook 'Scaffolded only' (code exists, never called by anything reachable); consensus_edge is a deliberate flag-off. The composite is 'Duplicate or conflicting implementation'.
(c) numericProof 'expected: 1' is not derived from anything in the repo — it is the audit prompt's product preference restated as a measurement. The falsifiable core is the 3-way threshold split, which I confirmed and quantified.
(d) blastRadius playersAffected 1072 is not measured. The population that actually experiences the split is 421 rows carrying a direction stamp, of which 140 (90 + 50) are surfaced inconsistently.
(e) 'reachable today' = 14 is a production claim, not a container one. In this container /api/bdvm/values returns no_projection_snapshot, /api/sharp/market and /api/sharp/roster-percentage return cohort_building, and /api/movers returns empty risers/fallers (historyDepthDays 0) — all pre-declared blocked-by-data. Today, here, roughly 9 emitters actually emit a verb. 14 is right for production; the record should say so.

PRIORITY: keep P1 for the rescoped core. Not P0 — both renderings are honest applications of different cutoffs to the same magnitude, so no single number is wrong; the defect is that two screens contradict each other on 90 top-of-board players with nothing saying which is authoritative. The architecture half (16 emitters, no arbiter, two dead consolidation attempts) is real but is a P2 design finding, not P1.
